title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
abstract: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.
summary: This paper proves a fundamental equivalence in quantum cryptography, showing that Entropy-Fixing Information (EFI) pairs are mathematically equivalent to expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS). By achieving a uniform characterization, the authors provide a deep quantum analogue to classical cryptographic relationships, solidifying the theoretical foundations of quantum randomness and security.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a uniform meta-complexity characterization for Entropy-Fixing Information (EFI) pairs, proving their equivalence to expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS).
main_result: The authors prove the equivalence $\mathsf{EFI} \Leftrightarrow \mathsf{1PRS}$, providing the first uniform meta-complexity characterization for EFI pairs and establishing a quantum analogue of classical cryptographic equivalences.
method: The core method involves removing non-uniformity from previous constructions, utilizing entropy gap analysis, local prefix witnesses, and the random-start idea to establish the necessary entropy surplus.
model_or_system: The work operates within the framework of quantum information theory, dealing with pure quantum states, quantum circuits, and cryptographic primitives like EFI pairs and 1PRS.
key_observables: Von Neumann entropy ($S$), algorithmic entropy ($H$), conditional entropy, and the entropy gap ($\chi$).
important_parameters: Security parameter ($\lambda$), expansion factor, and specific polynomial-time computable parameters ($L, N, t, \ell$).
main_assumptions: The proof builds upon established quantum information facts and relies on the ability to use local prefix witnesses and the random-start idea to remove classical advice.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the equivalence relationships between EFI pairs, 1PRS, svOWSG, and quantum commitments, forming a quantum analogue of classical cryptographic equivalences.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by building upon prior work, establishing the equivalence chain ($	ext{EFI} \Leftrightarrow 	ext{svOWSG} \Leftrightarrow 	ext{quantum commitments} \Leftrightarrow 	ext{1PRS}$), and culminating in the proof of the forward implication using entropy manipulations and witness constructions.
why_interesting: While highly abstract, the rigorous mathematical tools developed for bounding entropy and proving computational indistinguishability are foundational to understanding the limits of quantum computation and information processing.
